# dsh-win-control - Computer Control

DeepSeek Harness plugin that drives a Windows desktop: program-first automation
(window control, UI

Automation, browser CDP, local Windows OCR), humanised
mouse/keyboard input, and a live control pane

tomation, browser CDP, local Windows OCR), humanised
mouse/keyboard input, and a live control panel.
## Self-configuring and adaptive

On first activation the plugin probes the machine and writes its own config to
`<DSH_HOME>/computer-

control/config.json`: Windows version, PowerShell version, screen
size, OCR engine + languages, UI A

utomation availability, python/pypinyin. Every later
run reuses that file (re-read every few seconds

, edits are honoured), and each tool
adapts to it:

- no OCR language pack -> computer_find_text says so immediately instead of failing deep
- no python

+pypinyin -> typing mode "ime" goes straight to direct Unicode typing
- no UI Automation -> computer

_uia explains it; computer_act still uses OCR
- no browser on a CDP port -> computer_dom explains ho

w to launch one
- a Harness UI without the expected slots -> the panel is skipped, Host tools keep w

orking
- `computer_selftest` re-probes and rewrites the config on demand
## Browser pages are read, not scanned

- `computer_dom` speaks the Chrome DevTools Protocol directly (dependency-free WebSocket
client): re

ad `innerText`/`outerHTML`, run JavaScript, click a selector, navigate, or
launch Edge/Chrome with a

n isolated profile and `--remote-debugging-port`.
- `computer_page_text` reads the whole page throug

h UI Automation TextPattern, with a local
OCR dump as fallback.
- `computer_find_text` with an empty
`text` dumps every recognized line of any window.

Prefer HTTP (`web_fetch`) for public pages and the readers above for logged-in or
JS-rendered pages;
OCR stays the fallback for canvas, games and self-drawn apps.
## Install

Requirements: Windows 10/11 and a DeepSeek Harness build that can install profile bundles.
Everythin

g else ships with Windows (powershell.exe, user32/gdi32/imm32, UI Automation,
WinRT OCR).

# Computer Control (电脑控制)

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that lets the agent — and you — drive this Windows desktop:
screen capture
s, mouse movement/clicks/scroll/drag, and keyboard text or key chords.

One implementation, two callers: every button in the on-screen panel calls the same
Host operation t
hat the agent tools call, so the two surfaces cannot drift apart.
## Nothing is stored by default
There are three ways to look at the screen, and only the last one touches the disk:

1. **Panel preview (you)** — a persistent PowerShell worker captures frames into memory.
Host keeps

the latest frame in memory, the panel renders it from a Blob object URL and
revokes the previous URL

as soon as the next frame arrives. Zero disk writes; a frame
costs ~90–150 ms, so the panel refresh

es at 0.5 s / 1 s / 2 s.
2. **`computer_look` (the agent)** — the frame is captured in memory, saved

as a
*transient* attachment only long enough for one model call, and that object file is
deleted im

mediately after the answer. The agent receives text, never a picture, so
nothing accumulates in the

attachment library.
[该节后续省略]
## What it adds
Agent tools:
| Tool | What it does |
| `computer_act` | One operation, automatic route: UIA Invoke/SetValue when the control tree is rich

, else OCR + click. Reports which channel ran. |
| `computer_uia` | Inspect and drive the UI Automat

ion tree: probe, tree, find, invoke, click, focus, setvalue. |
| `computer_open` | Open a program, f

ile, folder or URL through the shell; returns the launched pid. |
| `computer_window` | List windows

(title, pid, hwnd, rect, minimized); focus / minimize / maximize / restore / close / move one. |
|
`computer_find_text` | OCR the screen or one window; returns matching lines with screen-pixel boxes
and centers. With `scroll: true` it keeps scrolling and re-OCRing until the text appears (pure OCR,

no vision). An empty `text` dumps every recognized line. |
| `computer_page_text` | Read a whole bro
wser page (or any window with a UI Automation TextPattern) directly: UIA text first, local OCR dump

as fallback. |
| `computer_dom` | CDP direct read: list page targets, read `innerText`/`outerHTML`,
run JavaScript, click a selector, navigate, or launch a debuggable Edge/Chrome (isolated profile). |
| `computer_click_text` | OCR-locate text (optionally inside a window, focusing it first) and click

its center; `scroll: true` scrolls until found, then clicks. |
| `computer_look` | Ask the model ab

out the screen; frame is released right after the call. |
| `computer_screenshot` | Capture metadata

only; `includeImage`/`path` are the explicit "keep it" options. |
| `computer_mouse` | `move`, `cli

ck`, `double_click`, `right_click`, `middle_click`, `scroll`, `drag`. |
| `computer_keyboard` | `typ

e` Unicode text or `press` one key / a chord. |
| `computer_screen_info` | Monitor bounds, cursor po
sition, foreground window title/rect/pid. |

Measured on this machine: `computer_find_text` on a window ≈ **0.2 s**; `computer_find_text`
with `s

croll: true` found a marker 180 lines down after **5 scroll steps (~9.5 s, 0 tokens)**;
`computer_ac

t` ≈ **1.3 s via UIA** (probe + Invoke) and ≈ **1.6 s via OCR**;
`computer_window list` ≈ 0.5 s; `co

mputer_open` ≈ 0.6 s. A `computer_look` costs ~10–25 s,
[该节后续省略]
## How it works

- `index.js` — Host half: the tools, `computer_look`, the prefix route on
`ctx.webServer`, the frame

worker, the transient-attachment lifecycle, cleanup, and the
dependency-free CDP client.
- `scripts

/screenshot-worker.ps1` — long-lived worker: one `Add-Type`/DPI setup, then one
JSON line per captur

e on stdin/stdout, PNG returned as base64.
- `scripts/computer-control.ps1` — one-shot helper for mo

use, keyboard, screen info,
UI Automation, page text (`pagetext`) and explicit file/region captures

(`SendInput` + `user32`).
- `client.js` — Client half: a `shell.overlay` entry with inline `zh`/`en`

dictionaries
registered through the Harness locale service.

Coordinates are physical screen pixels measured from the top-left of the primary monitor
(the helper
s mark themselves per-monitor DPI aware).
